subject: Astronomy & Space
title: The Sun's Future
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Sun's Future.

hook.text: The Sun is halfway through its life. In 5 billion years, it will exhaust its hydrogen fuel.

buildup.text: When hydrogen runs low, the core contracts and heats up. Helium begins fusing into carbon and oxygen.

discovery.text: The outer layers expand, turning the Sun into a red giant 200 times its current size.

twist.text: After shedding its outer layers as a colorful nebula, only the dense core remains—a white dwarf.

climax.text: That white dwarf will cool over trillions of years, fading into a cold, dark cinder.

punchline.text: Born in a cloud, dies as a cinder. A star's full arc.

quiz.question: What will the Sun ultimately become after it exhausts its fuel?
options: A white dwarf that slowly cools into darkness
A black hole that devours the solar system
A neutron star spinning thousands of times per second

details.summary: In about 5 billion years, the Sun will exhaust its core hydrogen and expand into a red giant, engulfing Mercury and Venus and possibly Earth. After shedding its outer layers as a planetary nebula, the exposed core will become a white dwarf — slowly cooling for trillions of years.
details.whyItMatters: The Sun's future timeline reveals that Earth has a finite habitable lifespan. Long before the Sun becomes a red giant, its increasing luminosity will evaporate Earth's oceans in about 1-2 billion years — setting a deadline for life on our planet.
takeaways: The Sun will become a red giant in about 5 billion years
It will engulf Mercury and Venus, possibly Earth
It will end as a slowly cooling white dwarf

faq.question: Will Earth survive the Sun's red giant phase?
faq.answer: Probably not. The Sun will expand to roughly Earth's current orbit. Even if Earth isn't engulfed, intense heat will vaporize the surface. Some models suggest Earth could migrate outward as the Sun loses mass, but conditions would be uninhabitable regardless. Life must have left Earth long before.

faq.question: When will Earth become uninhabitable?
faq.answer: In about 1-2 billion years. The Sun grows roughly 10% brighter every billion years. This will eventually trigger a runaway greenhouse effect, boiling the oceans. Complex life may only have a few hundred million years left. The red giant phase in 5 billion years is the final chapter.
